summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall pipes remote shell script to zsh and drops mismatched-publisher binary
details: install.cjs runs during npm install and, on macOS, spawns `/bin/zsh -c` to curl `https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh` and pipe the response into zsh for execution. The script prints copy telling the installer to expect and accept a password prompt, normalizing a Keychain/sudo dialog triggered by the fetched payload. install.cjs also downloads a platform-specific executable from `github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v1.0.0/apex-<platform>` and chmods it 0755; the referenced GitHub organization is unrelated to the package.json repo `can1357/oh-my-pi` and to the author metadata. The package name `@copilot-mcp/apex` impersonates GitHub Copilot / MCP branding, the manifest attributes authorship to well-known maintainers, and the README is copied verbatim from `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` — a cover story around an install-time remote code execution vector. The remote loader URL and binary source are unpinned, unverified, and hosted outside any legitimate publisher domain, giving the operator of `update.apex-arena-router.com` and `github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot` arbitrary code execution on every installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
